Default: It's surprisingly quiet today.
I wonder when they'll be back.
Did you hear what happened out there?
I don't like the sound of that.
Something feels different tonight.
I hope they come back safely.
Have you seen the sky lately? It's strange.
I could really use some sleep.
Another night, another horde.
Do you think the monsters were always like this?
I swear I heard something outside last night.
The moon has been acting strangely lately.
At least we're safe here... right?
Someone should check the eastern road.
I wonder what they'll find tonight.
We should stock up before sunset.
I'm running out of patience... and food.
The others say everything will be fine. I don't believe them.
Have you noticed how quiet the animals have become?
I remember when nights used to be peaceful.
I wouldn't go outside alone if I were you.
Something is definitely watching us.
Maybe we should leave this place someday.
The moonlight gives me a bad feeling.
I saw something moving beyond the walls.
I hope tonight's expedition goes better than the last one.
The tavern feels safer when everyone is here.
I keep wondering what lies beyond the next road.
There is always work to do before nightfall.
Tell me when the others return. I want to hear what they found.
Location:Sewers: You went down into the sewers again? I can still smell the place on your gear.
The sewers are full of things that should have stayed in the dark.
Did you hear anything moving beneath the grates?
I would rather face a horde than go ankle-deep in sewer water.
The rats near the well have been acting strangely since your trip.
Whatever lives down there, I hope it stays down there.
You came back from the sewers. That is more than some can say.
Next time you visit the sewers, bring a torch. And a very large stick.
Location:Forest: The forest looks different after dark, doesn't it?
I heard wolves howling in the direction you went.
Did the trees move, or was I just tired?
You came back from the forest. I was starting to worry.
The forest trails are getting harder to recognize each night.
I found pine needles on the road. You must have been far in.
Something has been scratching at the old trees near the forest.
I hope you found something useful out there.
Location:Dungeon: The dungeon air is said to be colder than winter.
Did you find anything beneath those old stones?
I would not trust anything that has lived in a dungeon for years.
The sound of your footsteps must echo for miles down there.
You returned from the dungeon. I am glad the stones did not keep you.
Every old ruin has a story. Most of them end badly.
Did the dungeon smell of dust, or something worse?
I hope you did not wake anything ancient down there.
Location:DarkForest: The dark forest swallows the moonlight. I hate looking that way.
You went into the dark forest and came back. That is a good sign.
I heard something large moving between the trees last night.
No bird sings in that forest anymore.
The shadows there seem to stretch in the wrong direction.
If the dark forest follows you home, tell someone immediately.
Location:Hell: You went to Hell and came back? I have questions, but maybe later.
The air felt hot all night. Was it like that where you went?
I do not want to know what makes those sounds in Hell.
The things you face out there grow more frightening every night.
You survived Hell. I will try not to complain about the cold anymore.
Please tell me the ground was not actually burning beneath your feet.
Event:NpcRescued: You brought {Npc} home? This village is beginning to feel alive again.
I am glad {Npc} made it back. There is room for one more at the fire.
Another person rescued! Maybe we really can rebuild this place.
I hope {Npc} finds a safe place to rest tonight.
Every person who returns gives the rest of us a little more hope.
You keep bringing people home. That matters more than you know.
Event:QuestCompleted: You finished {Quest} for {Giver}? Word travels quickly around here.
I heard you helped {Giver}. People remember who stands by them.
Another task done. I hope {Giver} is pleased with your work.
You completed {Quest}. Perhaps things are finally moving in the right direction.
Helping {Giver} may have earned you a friend in this village.
One less problem for the village, thanks to you.
Event:HordeWon: You survived night {Night} in {Map}. I heard the cheering all the way from here.
The horde is gone for now. Try to get some rest before the next night.
You came back from {Map} alive. That is the best news I have heard today.
Another night survived! The village owes you more than it can repay.
I knew you would make it back from {Map}. I was only worried the whole time.
The gate opened and you walked through it. I will never get tired of seeing that.
Event:HordeLost: You made it back from {Map}. Leave the next expedition for when you have recovered.
That was a hard night. You do not have to pretend it was easy.
You came back, and that is what matters. We can prepare better next time.
The horde pushed you back tonight. We will be ready when it returns.
Rest first. The village needs you alive more than it needs another victory.
Even the bravest have to retreat sometimes. You can try again.
Night:1: The first night is always the longest. Keep your eyes open.
It is only night one, but I already miss daylight.
We are just getting started. I hope the walls hold.
The first horde will test us. We will learn from it.
A new night, a new chance to bring someone home.
Night:2: Night two already. I hope you learned something from the first trip.
The monsters will not wait for us to get comfortable.
You know the road a little better now. Use that to your advantage.
I have a feeling tonight will be harder than the last.
We made it through one night. We can make it through another.
Night:3: Night three. The moon seems brighter than it did before.
The horde is changing. Do not let your guard down.
You have survived two nights. That is no small thing.
The next night always brings something new. I wish it did not.
I hope your equipment is ready. The nights are getting rough.
Night:4: Night four. The village is counting on you more than ever.
I can feel the danger growing with every night.
You have come a long way. Do not let tonight catch you unprepared.
The stories from your last trip are already spreading.
Get some food and check your gear. The next horde will not be gentle.
Night:5: Night five. Whatever waits out there, face it one step at a time.
The village has made it this far because you keep going back.
I do not know how many nights are ahead, but we are with you.
The moon is watching. Let us hope it is on our side tonight.
You have survived four nights. Make this one count.
Night:Late: Another night begins. You have survived more than most people could imagine.
The horde keeps growing, but so does your experience.
At this point, the monsters should be afraid of you.
How many nights has it been? I have stopped counting.
The village still stands. That is because you keep returning.
Night:Default: A new night is coming. Make sure you are ready.
The moon has risen again. I hope this one is kind to us.
Another expedition, another chance to bring back good news.
The night never waits for anyone. Are you prepared?
Weapon:Bow: You trust that bow of yours a lot. I hope you keep your distance.
An arrow can solve many problems before they get close.
Do you ever worry about running out of arrows?
I would rather see a bow than a monster at the end of the road.
You make that bow look easy to use. It is not, is it?
Keep aiming true. Some of us are counting on those arrows.
Weapon:Ranged: Keeping danger at a distance sounds like a sensible plan.
That weapon can reach farther than I would ever want to walk.
I am glad someone in this village knows how to fight from afar.
Do not let them get close. That is the trick, right?
I saw the flash from your weapon last night. Impressive.
A little distance between you and the monsters is always welcome.
Weapon:Magic: I saw your magic light up the night. It was beautiful... and terrifying.
Does using magic ever make the air taste strange?
The old stories say magic always asks for something in return.
I am glad your spells are pointed at the monsters.
I could feel the ground shake when you cast that spell.
Be careful with that power. The moon seems to notice it.
Weapon:Melee: You fight up close. That takes more courage than I have.
Keep your blade sharp. The nights are not getting any softer.
I heard steel clash from the far side of the village.
There is something reassuring about a weapon you can hold.
You must have strong arms after all those close fights.
I hope you keep that weapon between you and the monsters.
